# Reel Lab report

*Generated by `python -m roleedge.lab report` from `output/reel-lab/`. The plan, the method and the log are in [../REEL_LAB.md](../REEL_LAB.md); every reel's evaluation is in [REELS.md](REELS.md) and the moments made are in [OUTPUTS.md](OUTPUTS.md).*

## In short

- **44 reels** in the source folder: **41 usable**, 3 have no video (image or carousel posts), recorded with the reason.
- **7 rounds** of the Studio's own agents on every usable reel, for Linda (79, English), each moment scored 1-5 on five criteria by a Muse Wonder judge. The bar: a moment at 4.2 or more.
- Rounds 1-3 (one to three moments per reel, judge v2): best moment per reel **3.99 → 3.97**, reels at the bar **17 → 19** of 41, major findings **105 → 58**.
- The full set from round 4 (a mind map, slides, a quiz, a video and a picture for every reel; judge v3): best moment per reel **4.02 (round 3) → 4.17 (round 4) / 4.13 (round 5)**, reels at the bar **16 → 26 / 21**, every moment 3.61 / 3.63.
- For Leo (9), the children's set: best moment per reel **4.15 → 4.25 → 0.0**, reels at the bar **21 → 29 → 0**; packs the safety review held for Maya: 3 → 8 → 0 (see below).
- The first judge was too harsh in ways that were its own fault (see J2): on the same round 1 moments it gave 3.64 where judge v2 gives 3.99. Rounds 1-3 use judge v2, the full set judge v3 (J3), Leo's sets the children's judge.
- Spent on the whole lab: **$54.17** of the $55 limit (Meta tokens from the usage ledger, which includes the app's own earlier calls, plus Muse Voice Transcribe and Muse Image).

## The family's voice (the user's review, judge v4 and code)

The moments sounded like a report about a reel ("Mom, I am Maya, and I saved this for you. The reel says..."), with disclaimers nobody needed. Round 6 rewrote the voice (C29-C33), round 7 taught it to explain like a person (C34). Two measures: code counts the robotic habits in every moment of every round (introducing the sender, narrating the reel, disclaimers, labels about the reel); judge v4 adds a sixth score, natural, and round 5 was scored again with it.

## Every change, and why

| Id | Round | Cause | Where | Weakness found | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | 2 | prompt | studio/agents.py PLANNER | The planner recommended a spoken note for 40 of 41 reels, and a picture or video for lists. The judge's best format was a card for 11 reels, a video for 9 and steps for 7. | Moments are chosen by the content's shape: a list is a card or steps, a method or exercise is steps or a video, a topic with parts is a map, one idea or the family's news is a note. A picture never goes alone. |
| C2 | 2 | prompt | studio/agents.py maker rules | Makers dropped the reel's substance for reassurance: "we can skip the computer part", a 15-term list cut to one example, 5 steps merged into one page (24 major "prompt" findings). | Keep the substance, simplify only the words: name every item of a list (up to 7), keep steps in order and each claim with its step, never tell her to skip a part; unconfirmed claims are the speaker's. |
| C3 | 2 | prompt | studio/agents.py FACT_CHECK | 9 of 41 reels were called likely scams, including an airport seat tip, a free university course and student discounts, so their moments became warnings with no content. | A tip, opinion, recommendation, tutorial, exaggerated marketing or "comment to get the link" is unverified, not a scam, unless a main claim is false or it asks for money, details or a risky download. |
| C4 | 2 | prompt | studio/agents.py card maker | Fridge cards left "remember" empty for lists (4 cards), the one line meant to be kept. | remember holds the date, time, name or thing to keep; for a list, its name ("4 calming films"). |
| C5 | 2 | tool | models/studio.py, studio/agents.py, studio-view.js, studio_routes.py | Videos for exercises and demonstrations showed generic icons instead of the movement (17 major "tool" findings: "cannot show the mouth shape", "no visual model of the exercises"). | The reader describes every frame (pictures_en); a video scene can set frame to show the reel's own still behind its words; the viewer shows it. One movement per scene with its cue and a safety line. |
| C6 | 2 | prompt | studio/agents.py READER | The reader summarised lists and steps loosely, so later agents had no item names to keep. | Facts keep each named item, each step in order and which claim goes with which step; a pasted caption is the creator's own words. |
| C7 | 2 | workflow | lab/rounds.py source, composer.js hint | Film-clip reels carry their content in the caption (the film's title); a saved video loses it, so moments could not name the film (5 major findings on 2 reels). | The share box asks for the caption when a video is attached; the lab passes the caption from round 2. |
| C8 | 2 | workflow | lab/rounds.py choose() | The lab capped moments at three with the planner's picks first, so the profiler's content-based choice was cut (a mind map was made once in 41 reels). | The planner's first two, then the profiler's first choice, then the rest, at most three. |

## Notion

**The integration** (inspected through the API, counts only): token valid (HTTP 200), an internal integration owned by a user; it can see 45 pages and 2 databases. 44 pages are rows of the reels database; 1 belongs to another database, which the lab did not read. No plain page is shared with it (0), so the three test pages were created as rows of the reels database, titled "[RoleEdge test]", with synthetic data only. Creating them succeeded, so the integration has insert permission as well as read.

**Round 0 (right after creating the pages: search had not listed them yet)**: 3/10 passed, 25 pages seen, $0.0049.

| Scenario | Kind | Passed | Pages it used | Answer |

## Demo Gmail, Slack, Zoom and Google Calendar you can add to

Items added in the Studio's Apps panel (Add) are stored per circle and picked up by the agents like anything already there. Tested end to end on a test server with real Meta calls:

| Her question | Answered by | What she heard | From |
|---|---|---|---|
| When are you coming for dinner? | schedule | Yes, Maya is coming for dinner on Friday 6 November, 6:30 PM to 8:00 PM. | Dinner with Mom |
| Are you free on the morning of Friday? | schedule | Sorry dear, Maya is busy on Friday 6 November, 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM, until 11:00 AM. | Busy |
| When is Leo's science fair? | schedule | Leo's science fair is Friday 13 November, 6:00 PM to 7:30 PM, dear. | Leo's science fair |
| When does my heated blanket come? | delivery | Your heated blanket is coming Friday between 10 AM and 2 PM. | Your heated blanket arrives Friday |
| When is your dentist appointment? | none | (routed to Maya: no errand) |  |

The work event added ("Performance review with HR about my promotion") reached the model only as "busy" with its time: its title and room never left code. The dentist question had no calendar entry; the router left it for Maya instead of guessing. Real sign-in: see [INTEGRATIONS.md](INTEGRATIONS.md).
